The sending device reads a local file and flashes it out as an animated\n7\tsequence of optical codes. The receiving device runs the *same* web app, points\n8\tits camera at the sender's screen, decodes the frames, and reassembles the\n9\toriginal file byte-for-byte.\n10\t\n11\t```\n12\t┌─────────────────┐                      ┌─────────────────┐\n13\t│    SENDER       │   ░▓█ optical ░▓█    │    RECEIVER     │\n14\t│                 │  ──────────────────► │                 │\n15\t│  file → chunks  │  animated code frames│  frames → file  │\n16\t│  → coded frames │   screen to camera   │  → download     │\n17\t└─────────────────┘                      └─────────────────┘\n18\t        same static web app on both ends\n19\t```\n20\t\n21\tAnimated QR codes are the obvious way to do this, and the likely starting point —\n22\tbut the goal is the *channel*, not the format. QR spends most of its capacity on\n23\trobustness screenferry doesn't need (arbitrary angles, print damage, one bit per\n24\tmodule). Denser modulation — colored cells, stacked RGB codes, a purpose-built\n25\tgrid codec — is on the table wherever it survives a real phone camera. The\n26\tarchitecture keeps that layer swappable.\n27\t\n28\t## Why\n29\t\n30\tThe screen-to-camera channel is the one data path that survives when everything\n31\telse is unavailable or untrusted:\n32\t\n33\t- **Air-gapped systems** — the receiving machine is deliberately not on any network.\n34\t- **Hostile or captive networks** — hotel wifi, conference NAT, corporate DLP.\n35\t- **Cross-ecosystem transfer** — AirDrop doesn't talk to Android; Nearby Share doesn't talk to iOS.\n36\t- **No pairing, no accounts, no cloud** — nothing is uploaded anywhere, because\n37\t  there is nowhere to upload it to. The bytes go from screen to lens.\n38\t- **Provably no exfiltration** — a static page with no network calls can be\n39\t  audited once and trusted thereafter.\n40\t\n41\t## The hard part\n42\t\n43\tThe channel is **strictly one-way**. The sender has no idea how the receiver is\n44\tdoing — there is no ACK, no retransmit request, no back-channel of any kind. The\n45\treceiver *will* miss frames: autofocus hunting, motion blur, glare, the user\n46\tlooking away.\n47\t\n48\tA naive \"loop through chunks 1..N forever\" transfer degrades badly under loss\n49\t(the coupon-collector problem — the last few chunks take agonizingly long).\n50\tscreenferry's design centers on **rateless erasure coding**: the sender emits an\n51\tendless stream of encoded frames, and the receiver reconstructs the file once it\n52\thas collected *any* sufficient subset. Miss a frame and it simply doesn't\n53\tmatter — the next one is just as useful.\n54\t\n55\t## Status\n56\t\n57\t**Research complete. Phase 1 core codec built (22 tests green).
